title: Recognition of a binary hypersurface from minimal Jacobian minors
statement: Let $F$ be a field, $e\ge0$, $S=F[[z_1,\ldots,z_e]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $\mathfrak p=(z_1,\ldots,z_e)$ and $H=(h_1,\ldots,h_s)\subseteq\mathfrak p^2$. Put $R=S/H$ and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak p/H$. If $e\le1$, define $D=R$; if $e\ge2$, define $D\subseteq R$ to be generated by the $(e-1)$-minors of $(\partial h_j/\partial z_i)$, with the zero-ideal convention when there are too few columns [def-weil-matrix, def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant, def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. Assume $\operatorname{depth}(R)=1$ [def-weil-pbc-depth] and $D=\mathfrak m$. Then $e=2$. Writing $u=z_1$, $v=z_2$, there is a nonzero $f\in(u,v)^2$ with $H=(f)$. Its homogeneous quadratic part is $f_2=au^2+buv+cv^2$ for coefficients $a,b,c\in F$ satisfying $b^2-4ac\ne0$. Moreover $D=(\overline{f_u},\overline{f_v})$ in $R$, and the linear parts of these two derivatives are $2au+bv$ and $bu+2cv$, respectively. No restriction on the characteristic of $F$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), proof from the minor-order bound through the final quadratic-term calculation; Tag 0C48 (lemma-reduced-quotient-regular-ring-dim-2), part (2), for the principal equation.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete], $S$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ and residue field $F$. Since $H\subseteq\mathfrak p^2\subseteq\mathfrak p$, the quotient $R$ is nonzero and local with proper maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak p/H$: a class outside it lifts to a unit of $S$, and $R/\mathfrak m=F$. If $e\le1$, our convention gives $D=R\ne\mathfrak m$. Hence $e\ge2$.

source.place: Tag 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), minor-order bound in a minimal presentation and final quadratic calculation.

proof.text: The coefficient definition of differentiation [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative] shows that every $\partial h_j/\partial z_i$ has zero constant term, since $h_j\in\mathfrak p^2$. Thus these entries lie in $\mathfrak p$. If $e\ge3$, the determinant formula [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] puts every $(e-1)$-minor in $\mathfrak p^{e-1}\subseteq\mathfrak p^2$; the same inclusion holds when there are too few columns and $D=0$. Since $D=\mathfrak m$, taking inverse images in $S$ gives $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak p^2+H=\mathfrak p^2$. This is impossible: every element of $\mathfrak p^2$ has zero coefficient at $z_1$, whereas $z_1$ has coefficient $1$ there, by the multiplication formula of [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Consequently $e=2$.

source.place: Tag 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), minor-order bound in a minimal presentation and final quadratic calculation.

proof.text: Write $u=z_1$, $v=z_2$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] with $d=2$, $S=F[[u,v]]$ is regular local of dimension $2$. The ideal $H$ lies in its maximal ideal and $\operatorname{depth}(S/H)=1$ by assumption. Therefore [lem-trf-regular-surface-depth-one-principal] gives $H=(f)$ with $f\ne0$. Since $f\in H\subseteq\mathfrak p^2$, this is the required nonzero equation in $(u,v)^2$.

source.place: Tag 0C48 (lemma-reduced-quotient-regular-ring-dim-2), part (2), applied in the last paragraph of Tag 0C4C; power-series regularity: algebra.tex Tag 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary).

proof.text: Because $e=2$, the minors defining $D$ are precisely all the entries of the original Jacobian. Choose $a_j,b_j\in S$ with $h_j=a_jf$ and $f=\sum_jb_jh_j$, possible because both lists generate $H$. For $w=u,v$, the Leibniz rule in [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative] gives $\overline{(h_j)_w}=\overline{a_j}\,\overline{f_w}$ and $\overline{f_w}=\sum_j\overline{b_j}\,\overline{(h_j)_w}$ in $R$, since the terms divisible by $f$ or by $h_j$ vanish. These two inclusions prove $D=(\overline{f_u},\overline{f_v})$.

source.place: Tag 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), minor-order bound in a minimal presentation and final quadratic calculation.

proof.text: Let $a,b,c$ be the coefficients of $u^2,uv,v^2$ in $f$. Its quadratic part is $f_2=au^2+buv+cv^2$. By the coefficient formula of [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative], the linear parts of $f_u,f_v$ are respectively $2au+bv$ and $bu+2cv$; terms of total degree at least $3$ contribute only terms of degree at least $2$. Since $H\subseteq\mathfrak p^2$, the quotient map identifies $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ with $\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^2$. The latter has $F$-basis $u,v$: modulo $\mathfrak p^2$, every series of zero constant term is its linear part, uniquely. This follows directly by separating coefficients as in [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].

source.place: Tag 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), minor-order bound in a minimal presentation and final quadratic calculation.

proof.text:
Steps 4 and 5 and $D=\mathfrak m$ imply that the coefficient vectors $(2a,b)$ and $(b,2c)$ span $F^2$. Indeed, reduce an expression for either $ ar u$ or $ ar v$ as an $R$-linear combination of $\overline{f_u},\overline{f_v}$ modulo $\mathfrak m^2$; the coefficients reduce to their residues in $F$. Two vectors spanning $F^2$ have nonzero determinant: if $(A,B)
e0$ and $AE-BC=0$, division by a nonzero coordinate makes $(C,E)$ a scalar multiple of $(A,B)$; a zero first vector cannot span either. Hence the two-by-two determinant formula [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] gives $4ac-b^2
e0$, equivalently $b^2-4ac
e0$. This calculation is valid over every field, including characteristic $2$.

lean.statement: theorem minimalJacobian_binaryHypersurface (F : Type u) [Field F] (e s : ℕ) (H : Ideal (MvPowerSeries (Fin e) F)) (h : Fin s → MvPowerSeries (Fin e) F) (hgen : H = Ideal.span (Set.range h)) (hminimal : H ≤ (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin e → MvPowerSeries (Fin e) F))) ^ 2) (hdepth : Ideal.depth (Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk H) (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin e → MvPowerSeries (Fin e) F)))) (MvPowerSeries (Fin e) F ⧸ H) = (1 : ℕ∞)) (hjacobian : Matrix.minorIdeal e s (e - 1) (fun i j ↦ Ideal.Quotient.mk H (pderiv F i (h j))) = Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk H) (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin e → MvPowerSeries (Fin e) F)))) : ∃ (he : e = 2) (f : MvPowerSeries (Fin e) F) (a b c : F), f ≠ 0 ∧ f ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin e → MvPowerSeries (Fin e) F))) ^ 2 ∧ H = Ideal.span {f} ∧ homogeneousComponent 2 f = C a * X (Fin.cast he.symm 0) ^ 2 + C b * (X (Fin.cast he.symm 0) * X (Fin.cast he.symm 1)) + C c * X (Fin.cast he.symm 1) ^ 2 ∧ b ^ 2 - 4 * a * c ≠ 0 ∧ Matrix.minorIdeal e s (e - 1) (fun i j ↦ Ideal.Quotient.mk H (pderiv F i (h j))) = Ideal.span {Ideal.Quotient.mk H (pderiv F (Fin.cast he.symm 0) f), Ideal.Quotient.mk H (pderiv F (Fin.cast he.symm 1) f)} ∧ homogeneousComponent 1 (pderiv F (Fin.cast he.symm 0) f) = C (2 * a) * X (Fin.cast he.symm 0) + C b * X (Fin.cast he.symm 1) ∧ homogeneousComponent 1 (pderiv F (Fin.cast he.symm 1) f) = C b * X (Fin.cast he.symm 0) + C (2 * c) * X (Fin.cast he.symm 1)
lean.note: Uses the existing Matrix.minorIdeal (def-trf-minor-ideal), whose size-zero and oversized-minor conventions exactly give the stated D. Ideal.depth at the image of the variables ideal is the stated local depth. The existential equality he : e = 2 indexes the first two original variables by Fin.cast he.symm.
